findings.message: The configuration holds the key "seedPhrase", which names a seed, a mnemonic or a private key. The tool never reads one, and the value is not shown.
findings.fix: Remove the seed or the key from the file and from the history of the repository, and treat it as exposed: move the funds it holds to a new seed. The configuration lists paths only.

findings.message: The path m/84'/0'/0'/0/{index} of entry Bitcoin nested segwit has purpose 84, but the address type p2sh-p2wpkh is derived under purpose 49 (BIP-49). A wallet that restores the seed looks for p2sh-p2wpkh addresses under 49' and does not find these.
findings.fix: Change the purpose to the one of the address type, or the address type to the one of the purpose.

basis.text: The first level of a BIP-44 path is the purpose 44, hardened, and it says that the tree below it follows BIP-44.
basis.source: BIP-44: Multi-Account Hierarchy for Deterministic Wallets

basis.text: BIP-49 keeps the levels of BIP-44 and changes only the purpose, to 49, for P2WPKH nested in P2SH, so that a wallet that reads the P2PKH accounts of BIP-44 does not show these accounts by mistake.
basis.source: BIP-49: Derivation scheme for P2WPKH-nested-in-P2SH based accounts

basis.text: BIP-84 keeps the levels of BIP-44 and BIP-49 and sets the purpose to 84 for native SegWit P2WPKH accounts.
basis.source: BIP-84: Derivation scheme for P2WPKH based accounts

basis.text: BIP-86 keeps the levels of BIP-44, BIP-49 and BIP-84 and sets the purpose to 86 for single key Taproot (P2TR) accounts, so that a seed backup alone is enough to find them.
basis.source: BIP-86: Key Derivation for Single Key P2TR Outputs

findings.message: Entry Bitcoin taproot is on mainnet, but its path m/86'/1'/0'/0/{index} has coin type 1, which SLIP-44 keeps for the testnets of all coins. Mainnet funds sent to these addresses sit in the testnet subtree, where a wallet that restores the seed for Bitcoin does not look.
findings.fix: Use the SLIP-44 number of the coin on mainnet, and coin type 1 only for a testnet entry.

basis.text: SLIP-44 keeps coin type 1 for the testnets of every coin, not for one coin of its own.
basis.source: SLIP-0044: Registered coin types for BIP-0044

findings.message: The path "m/84'/0'/{wallet}'/0/0" of entry Bitcoin vault names {wallet} at level 3; the placeholders are {account}, {change} and {index}. BIP-32 writes a path as m and one index per level, each below 2^31 with a mark when it is hardened; the tool also reads {account}, {change} and {index} in place of a level. The other checks of the path were not made for this entry.
findings.fix: Write the path as BIP-32 and BIP-44 do, such as m/84'/0'/0'/0/0, or with placeholders, such as m/84'/0'/{account}'/{change}/{index}.

basis.text: Every key has 2^31 normal and 2^31 hardened children; a hardened index i stands for i + 2^31, and a path names one child index per level below the master key m.
basis.source: BIP-32: Hierarchical Deterministic Wallets

basis.text: BIP-44 puts five levels below the master key, in this order: purpose, coin type, account, change and address index.
basis.source: BIP-44: Multi-Account Hierarchy for Deterministic Wallets

findings.message: The path m/84'/3'/0'/0/{index} of entry Litecoin has coin type 3, but SLIP-44 registers Litecoin as 2. A wallet that restores the seed looks for Litecoin under 2' and does not find these addresses.
findings.fix: Change the coin type to the SLIP-44 number of the coin.

basis.text: SLIP-44 is the register of coin types for level 2 of a BIP-44 path, each used hardened: 0 for Bitcoin, 2 for Litecoin, 3 for Dogecoin, 60 for Ether, 61 for Ether Classic, 145 for Bitcoin Cash and 501 for Solana, among many more.
basis.source: SLIP-0044: Registered coin types for BIP-0044

basis.text: The coin type level puts each coin in a subtree of its own, so that one seed can hold many coins without the same addresses serving two of them; SLIP-44 keeps the list of numbers.
basis.source: BIP-44: Multi-Account Hierarchy for Deterministic Wallets

findings.message: The path m/44/3'/0'/0/{index} of entry Dogecoin derives the purpose without the hardened mark; BIP-44 hardens the purpose, the coin type and the account. A wallet that restores the seed derives other keys, and an extended public key above them with one leaked child private key gives away the parent private key.
findings.fix: Harden the purpose, the coin type and the account with ' or h, as in m/44'/0'/0'/0/0.

basis.text: In a BIP-44 path the purpose, the coin type and the account are hardened levels, and the change and the address index use public, that is normal, derivation.
basis.source: BIP-44: Multi-Account Hierarchy for Deterministic Wallets

basis.text: A hardened child can only come from the private key of its parent, while a normal child can also come from the extended public key; a parent extended public key together with one normal child private key gives away the parent private key.
basis.source: BIP-32: Hierarchical Deterministic Wallets

findings.message: The path m/44'/60'/2'/0/0' of entry Ethereum account 2 derives the address index hardened; BIP-44 uses normal derivation for the change and the address index. A wallet that restores the seed derives other keys, and the extended public key of the account cannot give these addresses to a watch-only wallet.
findings.fix: Remove the hardened mark from the change and the address index.

basis.text: In a BIP-44 path the purpose, the coin type and the account are hardened levels, and the change and the address index use public, that is normal, derivation.
basis.source: BIP-44: Multi-Account Hierarchy for Deterministic Wallets

basis.text: A hardened child can only come from the private key of its parent, while a normal child can also come from the extended public key; a parent extended public key together with one normal child private key gives away the parent private key.
basis.source: BIP-32: Hierarchical Deterministic Wallets

findings.message: The change level of the path m/44'/61'/0'/2/0 of entry Ether Classic is 2; BIP-44 uses 0 for the external chain of receiving addresses and 1 for the internal chain of change, and a wallet that restores the seed looks at no other.
findings.fix: Use 0 for receiving addresses and 1 for change addresses, or the placeholder {change}.

basis.text: The change level holds 0 for the external chain, the addresses handed out to receive payments, and 1 for the internal chain, the addresses that take the change of a transaction.
basis.source: BIP-44: Multi-Account Hierarchy for Deterministic Wallets

findings.message: The path m/44'/501'/0'/0 of entry Solana is for an ed25519 key, but the change is not hardened; SLIP-10 derives ed25519 keys through hardened levels only, so a wallet that follows it cannot derive this path at all.
findings.fix: Harden every level of an ed25519 path, as in m/44'/501'/0'/0'.

basis.text: SLIP-10 derives ed25519 keys with hardened children only, from a private parent key to a private child key; a normal child of an ed25519 key is not defined.
basis.source: SLIP-0010: Universal private key derivation from master private key

findings.message: Entry Solana as EVM is Solana, which takes ed25519 keys (ed25519), but its addressType is evm, one of EVM account addresses (evm); a wallet for Solana would not show this address. This is a best practice of this tool, not a rule in BIP-32, BIP-44, BIP-49, BIP-84, BIP-86, SLIP-44 or SLIP-10.
findings.fix: Choose an address type of the family of the coin, or correct the coin.

findings.message: Entry Bitcoin native segwit has a gap limit of 5, below the 20 of BIP-44: when a seed from a wallet that hands out addresses up to that gap is restored here, the app stops after 5 unused addresses in a row and does not show the funds on the addresses after them.
findings.fix: Set gapLimit to 20 or more, so that a seed restored from another wallet shows every address that wallet handed out.

basis.text: BIP-44 sets the address gap limit at 20: once a wallet meets 20 unused addresses in a row on an external chain, it takes the chain to end there and looks no further.
basis.source: BIP-44: Multi-Account Hierarchy for Deterministic Wallets

findings.message: Entry Bitcoin test is on testnet, but its path m/49'/0'/0'/0/{index} has coin type 0, the mainnet number of Bitcoin, not 1, which SLIP-44 keeps for the testnets of all coins; the test keys are then keys of a mainnet subtree, and one key can hold coins of both networks.
findings.fix: Use coin type 1 for testnet entries, or confirm that the app and the wallets it must match keep the mainnet coin type on this test network.

basis.text: SLIP-44 keeps coin type 1 for the testnets of every coin, not for one coin of its own.

findings.message: The key "gaplimit" of entry 7 is not one the tool reads, so its value was left out of every check. Did you mean "gapLimit"? The keys of entry 7 are name, coin, network, path, addressType, gapLimit, notes.

findings.message: The path m/44'/145'/0' of entry Bitcoin Cash has 3 levels below m; BIP-44, and BIP-49, BIP-84 and BIP-86 after it, use five: purpose, coin type, account, change and address index. A wallet that restores the seed under them does not look at this path.
findings.fix: Give the path the five levels of BIP-44, or confirm that the wallets the users restore their seed in derive the same shorter or longer path.

basis.text: BIP-44 puts five levels below the master key, in this order: purpose, coin type, account, change and address index.

findings.message: The entries under m/44'/60' on mainnet derive accounts 0 and 2, but not account 1: BIP-44 numbers accounts from 0 up, and its account discovery stops at the first account with no history, so a wallet that restores the seed may never find account 2 of entry Ethereum account 2.
findings.fix: Number the accounts from 0 with no gap, or use the placeholder {account} and let the app open accounts in order.

basis.text: Accounts are numbered from 0 up; a wallet should not open an account while the one before it has no transactions, and after an import it looks for accounts one by one and stops at the first that has no history.
basis.source: BIP-44: Multi-Account Hierarchy for Deterministic Wallets
